entries.rationale: Foundry already reaches the setting store through ProjectSettings::get_singleton() (fs_parser.cpp:136), which is exactly godot-cpp's shape.
non_mappings: core's GLOBAL_GET/GLOBAL_DEF macros appear nowhere in godot-cpp; ported code must spell ProjectSettings::get_singleton()->get_setting_with_override() (gen/include/godot_cpp/classes/project_settings.hpp:57,62).

entries.rationale: Engine-internal global-constant registry. The analyzer port reaches CoreConstants::* through src/bs_core_constants.h, which fails closed (every query returns false/empty) because godot-cpp does not expose @GlobalScope constants the way an engine module can. The include is dropped; the adapter is the audited contract.

Every ERR_* macro the port set uses is spelled identically in godot-cpp, so the thin macro shim predicted by docs/foundry-reuse-plan.md section 3 would be a rename-free wrapper and is declined. The seam instead #errors when a required macro is undefined, so a godot-cpp bump that drops one is a compile error rather than a silent no-op.
non_mappings: core's ERR_FAIL_* route through _err_print_error with a Godot Error code; godot-cpp's route through the GDExtension print interface. Message text and exit behaviour are not byte-identical, so diagnostics compared by a corpus must not come from these macros.

entries.rationale: godot-cpp has no Compression class, but it does have the same codec: PackedByteArray::compress/decompress take a mode enumerator that FileAccess spells as COMPRESSION_ZSTD. The shim is a rename over exactly that, and it keeps core's contract that decompression is told the expected size up front rather than growing a buffer.
non_mappings: core's Compression::decompress returns the decompressed length; godot-cpp's returns an empty array on failure, which is indistinguishable from decompressing to nothing. The caller compares the result size against the size its own header recorded, so a truncated or corrupt block is a data error rather than a short read.

entries.rationale: fs_cache.cpp opens script sources and compiled artifacts with FileAccess::open (fs_cache.cpp:407, fs_cache.cpp:511 at the pinned revision); the parse cache store adds get_file_as_bytes/store_buffer on the same class.

Absent from godot-cpp, and the four functions the tokenizer buffer uses split into two cases. encode_uint32/decode_uint32 are byte-order definitions -- core writes a uint32 little-endian, byte by byte -- so reimplementing them is exact rather than approximate. encode_variant/decode_variant reach the same serializer through UtilityFunctions::var_to_bytes/bytes_to_var, which is core's encode_variant with p_full_objects = false: the mode the buffer already asked for, because a constant is never an object.
non_mappings: core's decode_variant reports how many bytes one value consumed through an r_len out-parameter; UtilityFunctions::bytes_to_var does not, and the seam does not invent one. BSTokenizerBuffer length-prefixes each pooled constant instead, so the framing a reader needs is written down rather than guessed.

core's encode_variant can be called with a null buffer to size an encoding before writing it; godot-cpp's always allocates. The buffer writer appends the encoded block directly, so the sizing pass has no consumer here.

core's ResourceLoader::load is a static member (fs_parser.cpp:7488); godot-cpp's is an instance method on the singleton (gen/include/godot_cpp/classes/resource_loader.hpp:72,77) and drops core's trailing Error out-parameter. Call sites change, so this is a header mapping, not a call-compatible one.

entries.rationale: ResourceUID::ensure_path is a static member in both trees (godot-cpp at gen/include/godot_cpp/classes/resource_uid.hpp:65), so the one call site at fs_parser.cpp:1150 ports unchanged.
core reaches the Math:: free functions transitively through core/math/math_funcs.h; godot-cpp keeps them in core/math.hpp, so the seam includes both to preserve the single include.

godot-cpp's ClassDB forwards the engine's introspection methods -- class_exists, is_parent_class, class_has_enum and the rest -- onto the ClassDBSingleton binding (godot-cpp/include/godot_cpp/core/class_db.hpp:214), so the core spelling compiles unchanged and asks the engine the same question.
non_mappings: core's ClassDB::is_class_exposed() has no forwarded counterpart. It needs none: the ClassDB a GDExtension talks to is built from the exposed API, so class_exists() already answers it. The one port site that asked both (fs_parser.cpp:7569) now asks only class_exists().
core's ClassDB::has_enum() is spelled class_has_enum() in the binding.

entries.rationale: fs_warning.h reaches into core's object header for one type, PropertyInfo, which it uses to describe a per-warning project setting (fs_warning.cpp:203). godot-cpp keeps PropertyInfo in core/property_info.hpp rather than in a classes/ binding, with the same constructor signature and the same PROPERTY_HINT_ENUM hint, so the one call site ports unchanged.
non_mappings: core's Object, ObjectDB, ClassDB and the GDCLASS/GDVIRTUAL machinery in this header have no godot-cpp counterpart under this name; a GDExtension gets godot_cpp/classes/object.hpp and GDCLASS from godot_cpp/core/class_db.hpp instead. The port set touches none of them, so the seam maps only PropertyInfo.

PNAME(), which core defines in core/string/ustring.h:763 as (m_value) and fs_warning.cpp wraps around every warning name, marks a string for the editor's translation extractor. godot-cpp has neither the macro nor the extractor, so the port drops the marker at its call sites rather than the seam expanding a missing macro to nothing.

entries.rationale: core declares RefCounted and Ref<T> in one header; godot-cpp splits Ref<T> into classes/ref.hpp, so the seam includes both.
The port set only needs Script (Ref<Script>, Script::get_class_static()); core declares it alongside ScriptLanguage in one header, godot-cpp splits them.
non_mappings: ScriptInstance has no godot-cpp equivalent -- gen/include/godot_cpp/classes/ holds script.hpp, script_language.hpp, script_extension.hpp and script_language_extension.hpp and nothing else -- so the extension implements ScriptInstanceExtension instead.
Foundry's trait virtuals on ScriptLanguage are not in stock Godot (D5); BaristaScript owns its own trait registry.
core/object/script_function_state.h is engine-internal and is not reachable from a GDExtension; coroutines get their own suspended-frame object.

entries.rationale: SafeBinaryMutex locks through the engine's binary-mutex TLS machinery (fs_cache.cpp:168-174 at the pinned revision), which a GDExtension cannot register with. The port locks a plain std::mutex over the same critical sections, so no symbol of this header is referenced and nothing is mapped.
Same classification predicates over char32_t, relocated from core/string to godot_cpp/variant.

Absent from godot-cpp. Guarding it out was rejected: it would delete FSParser::TreePrinter, the parser's only AST dump. Vendoring Godot's MIT original was rejected on inspection rather than on principle: as_string() builds its result with String::resize_uninitialized, which godot-cpp's String does not have (it exposes resize, ptr and ptrw at gen/include/godot_cpp/variant/string.hpp:417,496,497, but no uninitialized resize), so the vendored copy would need editing -- and an edited vendor loses the upstream diffability that is vendoring's only advantage. The seam therefore reimplements the public API over String concatenation: the same observable behaviour, including the empty-append and empty-result rules, with a different cost profile. That is a shim, not an alias to a near-miss type.

The StringName type maps exactly, but SNAME -- used 39 times in fs_parser.cpp -- is a core macro with no godot-cpp counterpart. The seam supplies it with core's own semantics: a function-local static StringName constructed on first use. godot-cpp also omits core's StringName-versus-C-string comparison operators (core/string/string_name.h:82,84,197,198), which makes `name == "literal"` ambiguous rather than absent; the seam supplies the four exact overloads so the ported front-end's ~30 such comparisons keep their upstream spelling.

non_mappings: core declares vformat() in this header; godot-cpp declares it in variant/utility_functions.hpp, so the seam includes both to preserve the single include. fs_warning.cpp calls it 33 times.

godot-cpp's String is an opaque byte array dispatched through _method_bindings into the GDExtension interface, so it has no ptrw/resize/copy_from_unchecked and does not work without a loaded Godot runtime. No ported frontend code can be exercised from a standalone C++ test binary.

entries.rationale: Foundry's own addition. D1 gives BaristaScript one integer type, so the numeric tower is deleted rather than ported. The seam poisons the identifier so a surviving reference is a compile error naming the decision, never a stub that lets the tower creep back.

non_mappings: core/variant/container_type_validate.h, which Foundry extended with numeric_type and type_arguments, has no godot-cpp equivalent and is not mapped here; BaristaScript owns its own type descriptor (D2).

entries.rationale: Reached only under TOOLS_ENABLED, for editor colour and comment settings that belong to the editor-integration milestone. A GDExtension reaches editor settings through EditorInterface, not this header, so the seam maps nothing and the port drops the guarded block.

The `@rpc` annotation reads two enumerations through this include: MultiplayerAPI::RPCMode and MultiplayerPeer::TransferMode (fs_parser.cpp:8105-8158 @ c9d5e35). core declares MultiplayerPeer in scene/main/multiplayer_peer.h, which multiplayer_api.h includes; godot-cpp gives each class its own header, so the one upstream include maps onto two.

M1 guarded this out as debug-only and routed the decision to the warning milestone, which took it: the confusable-identifier check behind BSWarning::CONFUSABLE_IDENTIFIER (fs_parser.cpp:4898) is reinstated, because a warning code no consumer can raise is a code the registry lies about. The route is public -- TextServerManager::get_primary_interface() yields the Ref<TextServer> that carries has_feature(), spoof_check() and is_confusable(), the same three calls Foundry makes through the engine-internal TS macro -- so the engine header is not needed and only the bindings are. The cost is paid in build_profile.json, which now enables TextServer and TextServerManager; see src/bs_warning.h for the decision in full.
non_mappings: core's TS macro (TextServerManager::get_singleton()->get_primary_interface()) is engine-internal and absent from godot-cpp; ported code spells the two calls out. Foundry's other site, the keyword-confusable check at fs_tokenizer.cpp:672, raises a parse error rather than a warning, so whether to keep it stays a tokenizer decision -- the header it needs is mapped either way.

entries.rationale: godot-cpp exposes Engine as a singleton class; the analyzer reaches Engine::get_singleton() unchanged.
Upstream includes hashfuncs.h transitively for HashMap helpers. godot-cpp HashMap already pulls hashing; the port drops the include.

Upstream includes Node for TypedArray<Node*> and scene helpers. This analyzer slice checks Node ancestry via ClassDB / SNAME("Node") only. The build profile does not generate godot_cpp/classes/node.hpp, so the include is dropped rather than expanding the binding surface.

godot-cpp provides MethodBind for extension methods. Engine MethodBind* introspection is unavailable; BSNativeDB::get_method returns nullptr and D1 metadata is always NONE (bs_type_info.h / bs_native_db.h).

Foundry extended container_type_validate with numeric_type/type_arguments. BaristaScript owns its DataType descriptor (D1/D2); the include is dropped. Typed-container checks live in bs_type / BSParser::DataType.
godot-cpp mirrors type_info.hpp. FoundryTypeInfo numeric-width metadata is deleted by D1; bs_type_info.h keeps only METADATA_NONE.
